direct_answer: Yes. Shell discloses that it has “climate change transition plans” delivered through its strategy (ESRS E1-1 Transition plan for climate change mitigation) [Source 2], and that its energy transition plans are embedded in and aligned with its strategy and supported by financial planning processes [Source 11]. On 1.5°C alignment: Shell states it believes its net carbon intensity (NCI) targets are aligned with the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C goal and explains it derived its NCI targets from a filtered set of IPCC AR6 1.5°C scenarios, concluding this demonstrates alignment with the 1.5°C goal [Source 3]. However, the provided passages do not explicitly state that the overall transition plan (as a whole) is 1.5°C-aligned—only that certain targets/ambitions (e.g., NCI targets and an oil products ambition) are believed to be aligned/compatible with 1.5°C [Source 3].
compliance_rationale: Evidence clearly supports the existence of a transition plan for climate change mitigation (E1-1) and its integration into strategy and financial planning [Source 2, Source 11]. Evidence also supports a stated 1.5°C alignment claim for specific targets (NCI targets and oil products ambition) with methodological explanation [Source 3]. But the excerpts do not provide a clear statement that the transition plan itself is 1.5°C-aligned, nor do they provide enough detail to verify plan-level alignment beyond target-level assertions [Source 3].
disclosure_gaps: Explicit statement that the transition plan (not only specific targets) is 1.5°C-aligned, and the basis for that conclusion (plan-level alignment).
Quantified transition plan elements (key actions/decarbonisation levers) and how they map to a 1.5°C pathway (not present in the provided excerpts).
Time-bound milestones and progress metrics demonstrating implementation of the transition plan against a 1.5°C pathway (only referenced elsewhere, not evidenced in the provided excerpts) [Source 5].
Clarification of how differences in boundaries/definitions (e.g., NCI equity boundary vs ESRS boundaries) affect the 1.5°C alignment claim at plan level [Source 8].
key_findings: Shell discloses a climate change transition plan delivered through its strategy (ESRS E1-1) [Source 2].

Shell states its energy transition plans are embedded in and aligned with its strategy and supported by financial planning processes, with Board/Executive Committee involvement through annual planning cycles [Source 11].

Shell claims its NCI targets are aligned with the Paris Agreement 1.5°C goal and describes a methodology using IPCC AR6 1.5°C scenarios (filtering scenarios and deriving an intensity pathway) [Source 3].
Shell also states its oil products ambition is compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C, based on the same IPCC AR6 1.5°C scenario set [Source 3].
